english.title: Manufacturer / importer / supplier fail to supply revisions to safety information on substance handled at work premises

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[manufacturer]_
(B)_[importer]_
(C)_[supplier]_

of a substance, namely **(..SPECIFY SUBSTANCE..), failed to discharge your duty to take such steps as were necessary, so far as was reasonably practicable, that persons supplied by you with that substance were provided with all revisions of information provided by virtue of section 6(4)(c)(i) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974 as were necessary by reason of its becoming known that something gave rise to a serious risk to health or safety
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(4)(d) and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 2(2) of the Act for examples of the extent of the employer's duty.
(ii) Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector of the Environment Agency or the Natural Resources Body for Wales or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
